detailed_summary: The paper reports a cold-atom optical quantum memory that achieves near-unity storage-and-retrieval efficiency while simultaneously providing deterministic temporal adaptation of single photons between arbitrary input and output pulse waveforms. The system operates at high optical depth within a fully integrated architecture, enabling storage of photons with durations spanning over three orders of magnitude and arbitrary reshaping without compromising efficiency. This capability addresses the challenge of interconnecting heterogeneous quantum platforms that emit and absorb photons with widely differing properties, which currently limits inter-node interference and modular connectivity. By transforming a quantum memory from a passive storage element into an active programmable photonic interface, the work establishes a key building block for scalable entanglement-based quantum networks and modular quantum computing architectures.
